title: Putting Alcohol-Free Beer on Tap Pays Off for Pubs
paragraphs: When you think about someone going to the pub, you probably picture them having a beer or another alcoholic drink. But people can still enjoy drinks with friends at the pub while choosing to skip the alcohol.
And new research suggests that pubs may be able to make that choice easier without losing money.
Researchers from the University of York and Anglia Ruskin University studied what happened when three UK pubs made alcohol-free beer easier and more attractive to order.

Over nine months, the pubs tried three different changes. First, they added cans of alcohol-free beer to their fridges. Then they put up posters advertising the drinks. Finally, they replaced one regular beer tap with an alcohol-free option.

While promotional posters had little effect, making alcohol-free beer more available increased its sales. Sales rose particularly when it was offered on tap, with customers often choosing a freshly poured pint over a can.
And, importantly for pub owners, offering more alcohol-free beer did not hurt their profits from drink sales.

The researchers found that customers choosing alcohol-free beer were not replacing regular beer, however. Instead, it was sales of wine, spirits and soft drinks that fell when alcohol-free beer became available.
Perhaps surprisingly, weather seemed to matter too, with sales of alcohol-free beer rising when temperatures were higher.

The findings come as alcohol-free drinks grow more popular in the UK. A 2025 YouGov survey found that more than a third of UK drinkers had low- or no-alcohol drinks "regularly" or "occasionally" — and the trend was strongest among younger adults.

The researchers say offering alcohol-free beer on tap gives customers an attractive alternative without hurting a pub's business. They add that a change like this could help people cut back on alcohol without missing out on the social side of going to the pub.
